evidence_quotes.two_concerns_question: Joanna opens with 'aside from the pricing, do you have any other important concerns that you also want to discuss on this call?' — this is a non-standard open-ended format asked upfront, not the rubric's two-concerns version about movers showing up on time or damage to items. Customer responds 'No, just need to get a pricing,' so no concerns are raised.
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: N/A — customer raised no concerns at step 2.
evidence_quotes.value_days: Joanna says 'you're planning to do this move on the 11th of October which is a Sunday. I just wanna check are your dates flexible we're actually booked for that day but we do have an availability for the Saturday and the Monday.' Customer says 'I guess I can be flexible it's preferred but I think the Monday maybe an alternative.' Joanna does not identify a Value Day branch, does not quantify the dollar savings for Monday vs. Sunday, and does not ask about date flexibility again — the customer volunteered flexibility, but the structure of the rubric's value days behavior (identify correct branch, offer saving as total dollar amount, ask flexibility) was not executed.
evidence_quotes.rate_lock_then_ask: Never asked. Joanna provides pricing ($1,423 estimate including transportation fee), explains terms, and at the end says 'I'll send you that of course everything we've discussed right now. I get your car for a more personalized estimate just give us an inventory and we'll just review everything again okay, or photos are welcome as well.' The customer then asks to receive an email with details and promises to send inventory. Joanna never states a rate lock (quote is locked in, no price change), never mentions no deposit, and never asks 'Would you like our help with your move?' or any equivalent close.

top_strength: Joanna gathered detailed logistics efficiently — addresses, home size, bedroom count, specific items being moved, special handling concerns, packing preference, and box count estimate — and explained the all-inclusive pricing model clearly with concrete examples.
coaching_note: Joanna skipped the quid pro quo framing at open (time-boxed promise + dependable quote), omitted the Two Promises step entirely (On-Time Guarantee and No Worries Damage Coverage were mentioned only in passing within pricing, not delivered with permission lead-in or loop-close), never asked a final concerns check at step 6, and never asked for the business — the call ended with a request to email estimates rather than a direct close.
